description:
pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:151-184 (CrlChecker fields) tracks construction mode via two pieces of state:
- crl_issuer_cert: Option<Certificate>  (None = direct CRL, Some = an external signer cert is set)
- signer_discovered: bool                (true = signer came from path-level discovery, false = legacy explicit cRLIssuer or direct CRL)

A future contributor might suggest collapsing this into a single enum:
    enum SignerMode { Direct, Indirect(Certificate), Discovered(Certificate) }

That looks cleaner but changes the runtime cost shape: the match in check_revocation (lines 490-532) currently does `(&self.crl_issuer_cert, crl_declares_indirect)` which is a small enum pair. An enum-based redesign would force a discriminant check + cert dereference on the hot path.

More importantly, the two-bit state preserves the invariant 'signer_discovered = true implies crl_issuer_cert is Some' as a property check (lines 499) rather than as a type guarantee. That property is verified at construction time and never weakened — it's a small invariant easily reviewed. The enum redesign would couple the two bits into one type at the cost of making the IDP cross-check arms harder to read.

Defend: the current shape is intentional. The 'discovery bypasses the IDP cross-check' arm at line 499 reads as exactly what it is. The enum redesign would obscure it.
title: Two-bit construction state (crl_issuer_cert + signer_discovered) is the right shape
